description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:666-674

  fn may_set_custom_emoji(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
      _target_space_id: Option<&jmap_types::Id>,
      _op: EmojiSetOp,
  ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send {
      async { Ok(true) }
  }

The handler integration documented in the doc-comment (lines
640-642):

  /// On `Ok(false)` the handler maps to a `forbidden` SetError
  /// and skips the underlying mutation.

So a backend returning `Ok(false)` because 'site policy X: emoji
name must be alphanumeric' gets the same wire response as one
returning `Ok(false)` because 'caller is not a member of this
Space'. The client cannot distinguish.

Compare to apply_space_patch (backend.rs:399-405) which returns
`Vec<OpResult>` where each entry is `Result<Option<Id>, SetError>`
— backends can construct a rich SetError per op with description,
properties, server-set fields. apply_space_metadata_patch
(backend.rs:469-477) returns Result<Option<Space>,
BackendSetError<Self::Error>> with the same expressive surface.

may_set_custom_emoji is impoverished by comparison. The bool/error
shape encodes:

- Ok(true)  → permit
- Ok(false) → deny, hardcoded 'forbidden' description
- Err(e)    → server-fail, error propagated to JmapError

There is no path for 'deny with custom description'. A consumer
running a CustomEmoji policy that needs to surface a specific
reason ('emoji name conflicts with reserved system emoji set',
'caller has hit the per-tenant emoji quota', 'Space-scoped emoji
on this Space requires manage_channels permission') is forced to
either:

- Return `Err(e)` (which produces serverFail — wrong, this is
  a forbidden, not a server failure), or
- Return `Ok(false)` and accept the loss of the reason.

Engineering basis: the workspace has explicitly invested in rich
SetError responses elsewhere (jmap-server::SetError, the
with_extra builder added in JMAP-dha0). The may_set_custom_emoji
return type is a regression against that policy on a single
hook.

Recommended fix: change the return type to
Result<Result<(), SetError>, Self::Error>. The nested Result is
awkward but expressive — inner Err carries the SetError;
outer Err is the backend's own infra failure. Alternative:
Result<Option<SetError>, Self::Error> where None = permit and
Some(e) = deny with reason.

This is pre-1.0; the contract is still movable. Once a
downstream backend depends on the bool shape, this becomes a
major-version break.
title: API contract: ChatBackend::may_set_custom_emoji bool return loses deployment rejection reason
